raw_response:
I've been working this same ground on the Hebei plain for thirty years. 3 mu isn't much, but it's mine and I know every corner of it. The wheat-maize rotation is what everyone around here does — wheat goes in October, comes out in June, then straight into maize until September. No point changing what works.

**On wheat:** I'll use an improved variety, probably a Jimai-type that my seed supplier has been selling for years — good resistance to rust and stripe disease. I'll apply compound fertilizer as base at sowing, then chase it with urea at jointing. Four irrigations: sowing water in October because we can't count on rain, then winter water before freeze, jointing water in April, and grain-fill water in May. I'll spray once for weeds in winter, once for powdery mildew in spring. Rotary tillage after maize harvest to bury the stalks.

**On maize:** After wheat harvest I'll sow hybrid seed — Xianyu or Zhengdan, whatever the village supply co-op has. No-tillage directly into the stubble, saves labor with just the two of us in the house. I'll apply urea twice: base at sowing plus a big topdressing at tasseling. Summer rains usually help but I'll run the well at silking if it stays dry. One herbicide pass early, maybe one pass for corn borer if I see damage.
